args.report: Made the whole map harsher (settings are map-wide): the river is a trickle (2.2 blocks/s, was 3.6), the drought reserve is scarce, badwater is high, and there are a quarter fewer trees and berries. Moved the start upstream, 20% of the way down the river; I planted a berry patch and a grove beside it so it keeps its food and wood. Added a huge dam site 57% of the way down: a dam 4 tiles long would hold about 1,640 blocks, over 6 times a drought's need, and its water stays clean. Added a strong badwater spring (3 blocks/s) on the far bank from the start; its route drains into the river below the dam, so the reservoir stays clean. Trade-off: the weaker river fills that reservoir in about 13 minutes instead of 7. Assumptions: upstream means the upper third of the river; the opposite side means the far bank from the start. Every start rule still holds.

ended: Done, in one change. 1) Made the whole map harsher (settings are map-wide): the river is a trickle now (2.2 blocks/s, was 3.6), with longer droughts. 2) Moved the start upstream, about a fifth of the way down the main river; every start rule still holds (clean water at its level, enough trees and berry bushes nearby; I planted a berry patch and a grove to keep that true). 3) Put a large dam site about halfway down (57%): a dam there holds about 1,600 blocks and its water stays clean. 4) Added a strong badwater basin on the opposite bank; it drains into the river at 61%, below the dam. Trade-off: the weaker river fills that reservoir in about 13 minutes instead of 7.
